questions.text: What does 'tolerance' mean, as explained in the lesson?
options: Bearing pain or hardships with patience
questions.explanation: Tolerance means to bear pain or hardships with patience, and to bear things you do not like.

questions.text: At the conquest of Makkah, how did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) treat Abu Sufyan?
questions.explanation: He forgave Abu Sufyan and declared amnesty for those who took refuge in his house.

questions.text: Who did Allah send to the Holy Prophet (PBUH) after the people of Taif stoned him?
questions.explanation: Allah sent the Angel of the Mountains, who offered to crush the people between two mountains.

questions.text: What did the Holy Prophet (PBUH) reply to the Angel of the Mountains?
options: No; I hope their children will worship Allah alone
questions.explanation: He said no, hoping that Allah would let them beget children who worship Allah alone.

questions.text: For how many years did Hazrat Anas bin Malik serve the Holy Prophet (PBUH)?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Anas said, 'I served the Rasoolullah for 10 years.'

questions.text: According to Hazrat Ayesha, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) never:
questions.explanation: Hazrat Ayesha said the Rasoolullah never took revenge upon anyone.

questions.text: The word 'amnesty' means:
questions.explanation: Amnesty is a general pardon, as declared at the conquest of Makkah.

questions.text: Where did the kind old man in 'A Great Virtue' live?
options: In a small hut in a forest
questions.explanation: He lived all alone in a small hut in a forest.

questions.text: Who knocked first at the old man's door on the stormy night?
questions.explanation: The first visitor was a hunter looking for shelter.

questions.text: Who was the second person to knock at the door?
questions.explanation: The second knock was a farmer asking for shelter.

questions.text: Who came last, shivering with cold?
options: A woman with her two small children
questions.explanation: A woman came with her two small children, shivering with cold.

questions.text: Who told the old man not to open the door again?
questions.explanation: The farmer objected; afterwards he felt guilty and apologised for being selfish.

questions.text: How did everyone spend the night in the hut?
questions.explanation: The whole crowd spent the stormy night standing in the little hut, chatting.

questions.text: What great virtue did the old man show?
questions.explanation: The old man was kind and always ready to share with others.

questions.text: Who wrote the poem 'The Twins'?
questions.explanation: 'The Twins' is by Henry Sambrooke Leigh.

questions.text: Who mixed up the twins in the poem?
questions.explanation: 'As we were being washed by nurse, we got completely mixed.'

questions.text: What was the name of the speaker's brother?
questions.explanation: 'My brother John was named me, and I was named him.'

questions.text: The tone of the poem 'The Twins' is mainly:
questions.explanation: The poem humorously describes the confusion caused by the twins' likeness.

questions.text: The poet asks everyone: 'What would you do, if you were me, to prove that you were ___?'
questions.explanation: The poem ends: 'What would you do, if you were me, to prove that you were you?'

questions.text: Intonation is the:
options: rise and fall of the voice in speaking
questions.explanation: Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice in speaking.

questions.text: Henry S. Leigh was born in:
questions.explanation: Henry Sambrooke Leigh was born in London on 29 March 1837.

questions.text: Most people killed in road accidents, according to the lesson, are:
questions.explanation: Most of the victims of road accidents are young people below 30 years of age.

questions.text: According to research, about what percentage of traffic accidents take place due to drivers' mistakes or negligence?
questions.explanation: Almost 80% of traffic accidents take place due to the mistake or negligence of drivers.

questions.text: The most crucial factor causing road fatalities is:
questions.explanation: Over speeding is the most crucial factor causing fatalities or injuries.

questions.text: Violating a traffic law is:
questions.explanation: Any violation of a traffic law is an offence.

questions.text: By observing traffic laws we can avoid accidents, save lives and improve our:
questions.explanation: Observing traffic laws saves lives and improves our country's image.

questions.text: Who was the second Caliph of Islam?
questions.explanation: Hazrat Umar (RA) was the second Caliph of Islam.

questions.text: Hazrat Umar (RA) belonged to which tribe?
questions.explanation: He was born at Makkah Mukarramah into a noble tribe of the Quraish.

questions.text: For how long did Hazrat Umar (RA) remain Caliph?
questions.explanation: He remained Caliph for ten and a half years.

questions.text: Which reform did Hazrat Umar (RA) introduce to investigate complaints against state offices?
questions.explanation: He introduced administrative courts to investigate complaints against the offices of the state.

questions.text: How did Hazrat Umar (RA) treat the worship places of non-Muslims?
questions.explanation: The worship places and property of non-Muslims were given protection.

questions.text: Hazrat Umar (RA) gave great importance to:
questions.explanation: He gave great importance to justice and would not spare anyone in judgement.

questions.text: What does the proverb 'mens sana in corpore sano' mean?
options: A healthy mind in a healthy body
questions.explanation: The ancient Roman proverb means 'A healthy mind in a healthy body'.

questions.text: What is the national game of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Hockey is the national game of Pakistan.

questions.text: Through sports, young people learn values such as:
questions.explanation: Sports teach honesty, teamwork, fair play, respect and adherence to rules.

questions.text: Mental strength can be achieved through indoor games like:
questions.explanation: Indoor sports like chess build mental power; outdoor sports improve physical health.

questions.text: Between which years did Pakistan record extraordinary hockey conquests?
questions.explanation: Pakistan recorded extraordinary hockey conquests between 1956 and 1986.

questions.text: Sportsmanship means a commitment to:
options: fair play, ethical behaviour and integrity
questions.explanation: Sportsmanship is an understanding of and commitment to fair play, ethical behaviour and integrity.

questions.text: In the poem 'The Earth Speaks', who addresses the reader?
questions.explanation: 'The turning earth spoke in a somber voice.'

questions.text: What gifts does the Earth give us in the poem?
questions.explanation: 'Four seasons I give you,' the Earth said.

questions.text: According to the poem, spring is when the ___ bloom.
questions.explanation: 'I give you spring when the lilacs bloom.'

questions.text: In autumn, according to the poem, the maple is:
questions.explanation: 'I give you autumn when the maple is red.'

questions.text: What task does the Earth give the readers?
options: Use each season wisely, kindly and well
questions.explanation: 'Take my four gifts and use each one, use each wisely, kindly and well.'

questions.text: A figure of speech that gives human qualities to non-human things is called:
questions.explanation: Personification attributes human characteristics to non-human things, like the Earth speaking.

questions.text: 'He is a fish out of water' is an example of:
questions.explanation: A metaphor compares two things without using 'like' or 'as'.

questions.text: A simile compares two things using the words:
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as'.

questions.text: Who was Haji Usman?
options: A wise old man who settled quarrels
questions.explanation: Haji Usman was a wise old man respected for his piety, who often settled quarrels.

questions.text: Where was Haji Usman's village?
questions.explanation: He lived in a little village near Faisalabad.

questions.text: Who were the two men quarrelling?
questions.explanation: The two men were Haroon and Salman, his neighbours.

questions.text: What was the cause of their quarrel?
options: Salman's tractor destroyed some of Haroon's crops
questions.explanation: Salman had accidentally destroyed some of Haroon's crops by driving his tractor through his fields.

questions.text: What did Haji Usman do first to settle the quarrel?
options: Listened to both men in turn
questions.explanation: He knew he had to listen to them both in turn before deciding.

questions.text: In the poem about anger in Unit 8, which is a way to calm down?
questions.explanation: 'I can count to ten... I can breathe slow and deep' to calm myself down.

questions.text: Who first conquered Mount Everest in 1953?
options: Tenzing Norgay and Sir Edmund Hillary
questions.explanation: Tenzing and Sir Edmund Hillary conquered Mount Everest in 1953.

questions.text: Why is mountaineering called a risky sport?
options: It involves the highest risk and danger
questions.explanation: Mountain climbing is risky and dangerous, yet full of thrill and adventure.

questions.text: Which famous Pakistani climber lost his life attempting K2 in winter 2021?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Sadpara, who had climbed eight of the world's highest mountains, died on K2 in winter 2021.

questions.text: Why do climbers need artificial oxygen at great heights?
options: Oxygen becomes less, making breathing difficult
questions.explanation: As one climbs up, oxygen becomes less, so artificial oxygen is essential.

questions.text: How has training in proper equipment affected mountaineering?
questions.explanation: Training with advanced tools and kits has reduced the risks, though lives are still lost.

questions.text: What does 'dignity of labour' mean?
options: Equal respect for all forms of work
questions.explanation: Dignity of labour means equal respect for all work, including manual labour.

questions.text: According to the lesson, farmers are the ___ of every country.
questions.explanation: Farmers are the backbone of every country; they grow the food we eat.

questions.text: What would happen if farmers stopped cultivating crops?
questions.explanation: If farmers stop cultivating crops there will be famine and starvation.

questions.text: Which crops does Ahmad's father grow?
questions.explanation: Ahmad's father farms crops of wheat, barley and rice.

questions.text: Where did Ahmad's father study agriculture?
questions.explanation: His father received an agricultural education from Faisalabad Agriculture University.

questions.text: What did Saad and his sister make in the kitchen?
questions.explanation: Saad helped his little sister make a vegetable sandwich using a recipe.

questions.text: In Pakistan's flag, the white colour represents:
questions.explanation: The green colour represents the Muslim majority and the white represents minorities.

questions.text: When did Pakistan gain independence?
questions.explanation: Pakistan gained independence on 14th August 1947.

questions.text: What is the largest lake of Pakistan, according to Alia's article?
questions.explanation: The article lists Manchar Lake as the largest lake.

questions.text: What is the longest river of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The Indus River is the longest river of Pakistan.

questions.text: What is the height of K-2 given in the article?
questions.explanation: Highest Mountain: K-2, 8,611 m.

questions.text: Which dam of Pakistan is the world's largest earth-filled dam?
questions.explanation: Tarbela Dam is the world's largest earth-filled dam.

questions.text: Which of these is NOT listed among the top places to visit in the article?
questions.explanation: The list includes Swat, Hunza, Yarkhun and Kalash Valleys and Margala Hills.

questions.text: What is the official name of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: The official name is the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
